_metadata.description: RI-M7: the known-absent arm of the retrieval score-distribution census. Every question names one FABRICATED, specific causal-inference method/test/bound/dataset (an invented surname-pair plus a genuine methodological role -- 'estimator', 'test', 'bound', ...) that does not exist in the published literature and therefore cannot be present in ANY corpus, including this one -- a stronger absence guarantee than picking a real but supposedly-uncovered topic out of a ~12k-paper corpus would give. Framed as a natural, specific research question so retrieval is exercised the same way an answerable question is (plausible causal-inference vocabulary, a well-formed methodological ask) -- NOT a topic-absent question in eval_equation_slice_topic_absent.json's sense (that fixture's answers ARE in the corpus; this fixture's are not, by construction).
_metadata.structure: Array of records keyed by question_id, self-contained (question_text inline, same shape as eval_equation_slice.json -- no blind-file join needed). source_paper_id is JSON null: there is no gold paper, by design, so app/retrieval_eval.py's paper-level hit rule (result.paper_id in gold_paper_ids) can never fire a false hit against a real paper_id. fabricated_entity is the exact term the absence check (test_eval_known_absent_invariants.py) searches for; fabrication_kind is the methodological role assigned to it, for provenance/diversity bookkeeping only (not scored).
_metadata.provenance: Each fabricated_entity is an invented two-part surname (no connection to any real researcher intended or checked beyond the corpus search below) paired with a real methodological role, covering a spread of causal-inference subareas (staggered DiD, weak-IV, double ML, partial identification, synthetic control, causal discovery, regression discontinuity, missing data, conditional-independence testing, network interference, causal forests, transportability, external validity, mediation, adaptive trial design, instrument selection, exclusion-restriction testing, sensitivity analysis, dose-response) so the known-absent arm is not concentrated in one corner of the topic space. Each question_text was then written as a genuine, specific methodological question about that fabricated entity -- the kind a researcher would ask if the method were real -- so the retrieval system is exercised the same way an answerable question exercises it (real causal-inference vocabulary, a well-formed ask), not with an obviously off-topic or nonsensical string.
_metadata.absence_verification: Verified 2026-08-22 against the real ingested corpus DB (research-system-rag-data/papers.db, 12,390 papers / 399,676 chunks / 2,720,572 blocks, read-only): a case-insensitive SQL LIKE search for each record's exact fabricated_entity substring against papers.title, papers.abstract, chunks.text, AND blocks.text returned ZERO rows for all 24 entities -- not merely 'no paper about this,' but the literal term string never occurs anywhere in the corpus's own text. Because every entity is a fabricated name (not a real, possibly-obscure method this corpus happens to lack), this is a stronger claim than 'not covered by these 12,390 papers': it cannot be present in any corpus, so a future corpus refresh does not need to re-litigate the 'plausibly real but rare' judgment call a genuine-topic absence arm would carry. The same search is re-run mechanically (not just claimed) by test_eval_known_absent_invariants.py's DB cross-check tier, which skips (not fails) when papers.db isn't present near the checkout -- see that file's docstring for why, same posture as eval_equation_slice.json's own DB tier. A later corpus re-ingest that happened to introduce a paper using one of these exact invented terms (vanishingly unlikely, but not impossible for a common surname pair) would be caught by that tier, not silently poison the census.

ground_truth.question_text: What is the closed-form asymptotic variance of the Kestrel-Odom double-difference estimator under staggered treatment adoption with heterogeneous cohort sizes?
How does the Vantresca stability test detect violations of the parallel trends assumption in a difference-in-differences design?
What moment condition does the Halvorsen-Bijl instrument impose to achieve identification under many weak instruments?
What bias term does the Corrigan-Ashby debiasing correction remove from inverse-propensity-weighted estimators when the propensity model is misspecified?
How is the Petrenko orthogonal score test constructed to achieve Neyman orthogonality in a double machine learning pipeline with high-dimensional nuisance parameters?
What is the width of the Sablefeld bound for the average treatment effect under a monotone instrumental variable assumption?
How does the Quennell synthetic control weighting scheme penalize donor units with high pre-treatment volatility?
What independence test does the Draventis algorithm use to orient edges in the presence of latent confounders?
What is the Torvald-Meng correction factor applied to optimal bandwidth selection in a fuzzy regression discontinuity design?
How does the Ostrowicz partial identification bound tighten worst-case treatment effect bounds under nonignorable missingness?
What is the asymptotic distribution of the Chenoweth-Rudkin test statistic used to test conditional independence in a causal graphical model?
How does the Larkspur estimator adjust for network interference when estimating heterogeneous treatment effects?
What splitting rule does the Bellcastle instrumental forest use to estimate heterogeneous local average treatment effects?
How does the Marchetti-Vann calibration procedure reweight a source population to support transportability of a causal estimate to a target population?
What does the Grunfeldt stability index measure when assessing the external validity of an estimated treatment effect across sites?
What weighting scheme does the Ilinca doubly robust estimator use to remain consistent under nonignorable missing outcomes?
What structural hamming distance do causal discovery algorithms achieve on the Tovarik benchmark dataset?
How does the Whitlock-Fenn corrected variance estimator adjust cluster-robust standard errors when the number of treated clusters is small?
How does the Amsterdam-Kilbride effect decomposition separate the natural direct and indirect effects when the mediator is affected by treatment-induced confounding?
How does the Rostova design adapt treatment allocation probabilities in response to interim causal effect estimates?
What criterion does the Feringhetti procedure use to select a valid instrument from a large set of candidate instruments?
What overidentification statistic does the Solenberg test use to assess violations of the exclusion restriction?
How is the Kranholt bound derived to quantify the sensitivity of an estimated causal effect to unmeasured confounding?
What kernel does the Petrossian estimator use to estimate the dose-response function for a continuous treatment?
